input.quote: shall be furnished and maintained on terms and conditions which shall be no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier for transmission facilities of similar type and quantity transiting the location involved
input.rationale: The only "no less favorable" / non-discrimination mechanics in the Agreement run against us, not in our disfavour. Subparagraph 15.2 (p0220) imposes the "no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier" standard on "The Terminal Parties" (per 15.1, p0219), and Subparagraph 17.2 (p0225) imposes the "reasonable and non-discriminatory" standard on "the Terminal Party" in respect of Direct Access arrangements. Paragraph 4.1 (p0107) identifies the Terminal Parties for Segments T1-T10 as SingTel, TM, CWHKTI, China Telecom, KT, NTT Com, KDD, Chunghwa Telecom and PLDT; Teleglobe USA Inc. is an Initial Party (p0053) but is not a Terminal Party, so it is not an obligor under either clause. As a non-Terminal Party acquiring transiting/inland facilities and Direct Access, we are a beneficiary of this MFN-style protection. Additionally, on the sell side, Subparagraphs 12.20-12.22 (p0206-p0208) expressly make the terms and pricing of our IRU/capacity sales "bilateral matters between granting Party and purchaser" and permit sales "on any commercial basis without any restrictions" — no obligation to extend best terms to the other Parties. I found no clause anywhere requiring us to offer any counterparty terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, or to match third-party offers. This therefore meets the preferred position (no MFN obligation on Customer), and the MFN in our favour is welcome; per the detection guidance we mark it compliant and do not redline. Noted only in passing: the 15.2 comparison is limited to facilities "of similar type and quantity", which is a like-for-like qualifier on the obligor's side and does not burden us.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
